sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836

items.q: In the JAK–STAT pathway, ligand binding and dimerisation lead to phosphorylation of which protein?
items.exp: JAK–STAT: ligand binding → dimerisation → phosphorylation of STAT protein → nucleus → transcription. (Book p836)

items.q: The hormones that use JAK receptors are:
items.exp: JAK receptors are used by growth hormone, prolactin (twin hormones) and erythropoietin (EPO). (Book p836)

items.q: Which two hormones are labelled the ‘twin hormones’?
items.exp: Growth hormone and prolactin are grouped as the twin hormones (both JAK). (Book p836)

items.q: JAK2 mutations are present in which group of disorders?
opts: Polycythaemia rubra vera, primary myelofibrosis, essential thrombocytosis
items.exp: JAK2 mutations occur in polycythaemia rubra vera, primary myelofibrosis and essential thrombocytosis. (Book p836)

items.q: The serine–threonine kinase receptor (STKR) acts by phosphorylating:
items.exp: STKR signals via phosphorylation of SMAD protein. (Book p836)
STKR hormones: activin, inhibin, BMP (bone morphogenetic protein) and TGF-β. (Book p836)

items.q: The most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine is:
items.exp: TGF-β is the most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine (TGF: stroke master). (Book p836)
